text:
support_jane: Heads-up — AcmeCorp hit intermittent 429s on POST /v1/generate around 09:00-09:12 UTC. They say no client change. Customer provided a few logs, attaching key headers below.

alex: Thanks. Can you paste one example request_id and the response headers (X-RateLimit-*, Retry-After, X-Tenant-ID, model)? That will help attribute which limit fired.

support_jane: request_id=rc-20240315-82b9, tenant=acme, route=/v1/generate, model=gpt4o-mini, status=429
Response headers: X-RateLimit-Limit: 120000, X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0, X-RateLimit-Reset: 1710551500, Retry-After: 2, X-Burst-Window-Used: 1024
Sample repro curl they ran:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" \
  -H "X-Tenant-ID: acme" \
  -d '{"input":"Hello world","max_tokens":512}'
```

alex: Given X-RateLimit-Remaining=0 + Retry-After suggests a tenant-level quota hit, but we should confirm if route or model-specific throttles are enabled for this tenant. Also want to check tail of requests/sec and burst usage during spike.

maria: Quick observability suggestion: run a PromQL-like query to get a 5m window breakdown by tenant/route/model. Example: 
```
sum by (tenant, route, model) (increase(redwood_rate_limit_denied_total{code=\"429\"}[5m]))
```
That gives counts of denied requests. Then correlate with:
```
sum by (tenant, route, model) (increase(redwood_tokens_consumed_total[5m]))
```
to see if a token hotspot caused burst window to exhaust.

ricardo: Also add a 1m rate for successful requests to detect traffic surges: 
```
sum by (tenant, route) (rate(redwood_requests_total[1m]))
```
Combine with `topk(10, ...)` to surface top offending tenants/routes.

anna: For quick triage dashboard tiles we should add: top 10 tenants by 429s (5m), top routes by 429 ratio (429 / requests), and max burst-window-used per tenant. Add an annotation for the customer-reported window (09:00-09:12).

support_jane: I looked at the tenant billing view — no sudden billing change. They use dedicated burst credits but it looks like the burst window was exhausted for ~3m. Their client concurrently spun up a fanout of small requests (many prompts with max_tokens=512).

alex: Actionable next steps:
- Maria: create a Grafana panel for `denied_by_tenant_route_model` and a dashboard link to paste to the customer.
- Ricardo: create an alert that fires when tenant 429 rate > 50 reqs/min or 429 ratio > 5% for 5m. Set severity=P2.
- Anna: add tenant burst-window-used metric to the billing/fleet dashboard and document sample queries in playbook.
- Support/Jane: ask Acme for client-side concurrency and exact time window + any SDK changes.

maria: I'll add the panel and include a drilldown link that filters by `tenant=acme`. Suggest adding a dashboard variable `tenant` so SRE/support can switch tenants quickly.

ricardo: For attribution to model variant, ensure we tag requests with `model` label in the ingestion pipeline. If missing, we need a quick enrichment job that maps request_id -> model from request logs.

alex: If enrichment is needed, provide a minimal repro step to Acme so we can reproduce in staging: 1) set concurrency to 50, 2) run the same payload with `max_tokens=512` for 2 minutes, 3) include bearer token and tenant header. If staging reproduces, we can test burst window behaviour safely.

support_jane: I'll ask Acme for those repro steps and share the repro ticket. Meanwhile attaching the grafana filter I made for now: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/limits/tenant-throttle?var-tenant=acme (temp link).

sre-bot: Incident note created — #INC-2024-4556, severity=P3, assigned to @maria for dashboard and @ricardo for alerting.

maria: Created dashboard panel, added `topk(10, sum by (tenant, route, model) (increase(redwood_rate_limit_denied_total{code=~\"429\"}[5m])))`. Pasting link: https://grafana.internal/d/abc123/limits (shared with support).

support_jane: Customer confirmed they had an automated job that ramped to 120 concurrent requests for ~90s at 09:02. They will throttle client-side while we add guardrails.

alex: Closing loop: once alert + dashboard in place we should follow up with product to discuss per-route soft-throttles or graceful 429s with richer `X-RateLimit` metadata (per-model). For now, support to advise client-side concurrency limits and add tenant-level alerting.

ricardo: I'll put the alert runbook in the playbook repo and link it from the dashboard.

support_jane: Thanks all — I'll update Acme and move to resolved if they confirm client change. :thumbsup:

anna: Nice triage. Adding note to postmortems channel if this recurs.

alex: Thanks team, great coordination.
